title: S7 Exchange and Deliverable Declaration Fields

entries.name: Stable deliverable identity
entries.requirement: Each project deliverable declaration shall carry a stable project identifier that remains traceable across the BEP, exchange schedule, issue records, and transmittals.

entries.name: Deliverable name or description
entries.requirement: Each declared deliverable shall state what information container, package, dataset, federation, drawing set, report, or other governed output is being delivered.

entries.name: Deliverable type
entries.requirement: Each deliverable shall identify its governed deliverable category or type and reference the applicable S7 deliverable-type vocabulary where one exists.

entries.name: Project phase or stage
entries.requirement: The project phase, stage, or appointment context to which the deliverable applies shall be declared explicitly.

entries.name: Intended use
entries.requirement: Each deliverable shall declare the purpose for which the receiving party may use the information.

entries.name: LOD/LOI or information-need basis
entries.requirement: Where level of information need is material, the deliverable declaration shall reference the applicable S2 requirement or project-declared LOD/LOI basis.

entries.name: Required exchange format
entries.requirement: The required file, dataset, or platform format shall be declared at project level; source examples such as RVT, IFC, NWD, PDF, or spreadsheets are not universal defaults.

entries.name: CDE location or governed destination
entries.requirement: The intended governed location, container path, or state destination shall be declared by reference to the applicable S3/CDE configuration.

entries.name: Review route
entries.requirement: The project declaration shall identify the applicable review route or workflow reference before issue or reliance.

entries.name: Acceptance authority reference
entries.requirement: Acceptance or sign-off authority shall be referenced from the applicable S1/BEP/RACI authority source rather than inferred from deliverable type or file format.

entries.name: Exchange milestone or event
entries.requirement: Each planned formal exchange shall identify the milestone, exchange event, or contractual context to which it belongs.

entries.name: Date or exchange window
entries.requirement: The project exchange schedule shall declare the applicable date or bounded exchange window; dates are project-specific and are not enterprise defaults.

entries.name: Exchange trigger
entries.requirement: Each exchange shall identify the event, contractual condition, coordination cycle, or other trigger that causes the exchange to occur.

entries.name: Originating and receiving parties
entries.requirement: The parties participating in the exchange shall be identifiable, including originating and receiving responsibilities where applicable.

entries.name: Expected deliverable references
entries.requirement: Each exchange event shall reference the deliverable identities expected within that exchange rather than restating them ambiguously.

entries.name: Issue/transmittal record reference
entries.requirement: Formal exchange shall be traceable to the applicable issue or transmittal record so technical movement is not mistaken for formal delivery.

entries.name: Constraints, dependencies, or limitations
entries.requirement: Material constraints, dependencies, permitted-use limitations, or rescheduling conditions shall be declared where they affect reliance or exchange execution.

non_promoted_source_content: Source example deliverable IDs such as DL-001 and DL-002 are examples only.
Example file formats, milestones, dates, parties, CDE paths, and role labels are project-specific and are not promoted as enterprise defaults.
The registry defines the required declaration structure; actual project deliverable lists and exchange schedules remain BEP/project artifacts.

provenance.source_title: BEP Template Scaffold for GAP-S7-01 Deliverables and Exchange Schedules
provenance.migration_note: Migrated the source scaffold into machine-readable declaration fields while preserving the source boundary that project deliverable lists and exchange schedules belong in the BEP rather than the S7 L4 standard.
